author: l. c. edmonds
title: Tennessee beats South Carolina by double digits to secure fifth straight season with over twenty wins - Knox Times
text:
The University of Tennessee men’s basketball team secured a 78-59 win over South Carolina on Tuesday at Colonial Life Arena. The Volunteers, ranked No. 23/25, improved their record to 21-9 overall and 11-6 in SEC play.
Tennessee played without freshman forward Nate Ament due to a right leg injury. Despite his absence, the Volunteers led for nearly the entire game and built a lead as large as 20 points.
Redshirt sophomore J.P. Estrella led all scorers with 22 points on 10-of-13 shooting, also contributing seven rebounds and three assists. Senior Felix Okpara matched his career high with 20 points and grabbed eight rebounds, while senior guard Ja’Kobi Gillespie set a new personal best with 12 assists alongside eight points and two steals.
South Carolina (12-18, 3-14 SEC) was led by Meechie Johnson’s 20 points and four assists, while Nordin Kapic added 13 points for the Gamecocks.
Tennessee shot over 54 percent from the field and dominated inside with a season-high of 56 paint points compared to South Carolina’s 18. The Volunteers also recorded a season-best 15 dunks during the game.
Head coach Rick Barnes reached another milestone with his victory total now at 857, surpassing John Calipari for first place among active Division I head coaches and moving into ninth all-time among coaches with at least ten years in Division I. “Barnes also registered his 123rd victory in SEC play, eclipsing Rick Stansbury for sole possession of No. 17 on the all-time conference-only leaderboard.”
With this win, Tennessee now holds a historical advantage over South Carolina in their series matchups and has won five out of its last seven road games against them.
The Volunteers will close out their regular season Saturday when they host Vanderbilt at Food City Center.
